record.original_question: For each n > 3, determine the smallest integer μ(n) such that any convex plane curve run μ(n) times admits arbitrarily small perturbations as a nondegenerate closed curve in ℝn, and decide whether every regular closed curve in ℝn has Frenet-frame length strictly greater than μ(n) times the length of the standard closed geodesic SO(2) ⊂ O(n).

evidence.quote: An important open problem is to find µ(n) for n > 3 and to check if the length of the Frenet frame of any regular curve in Rn is greater than the length of SO(2) ⊂ O(n) multiplied by µ(n).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n>3$. A smooth closed curve $\gamma:S^1\to\mathbb{R}^n$ is called nondegenerate if at every point the derivatives $\gamma'(t),\gamma''(t),\ldots,\gamma^{(n)}(t)$ are linearly independent; equivalently, $\gamma$ admits a well-defined Frenet $n$-frame, viewed as a closed curve $F_\gamma:S^1\to O(n)$. A convex plane curve is a smooth simple closed curve in $\mathbb{R}^2\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ bounding a convex region; "running it $k$ times" means the $k$-fold cover $S^1\to S^1\to\mathbb{R}^n$. Let $SO(2)\subset O(n)$ denote the standard closed geodesic (a great circle of length $2\pi\sqrt{2}$ in $O(n)$ with its bi-invariant Riemannian metric).

Define $\mu(n)$ to be the smallest positive integer $k$ such that, for every convex plane curve $C\subset\mathbb{R}^2\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, the $k$-fold covering of $C$ admits arbitrarily $C^\infty$-small perturbations that are nondegenerate closed curves in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

(a) Determine $\mu(n)$ explicitly for every $n>3$.

(b) Decide whether, for every regular (i.e. nondegenerate) closed curve $\gamma$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, the length of the Frenet frame $F_\gamma$ in $O(n)$ is strictly greater than $\mu(n)$ times the length of the standard closed geodesic $SO(2)\subset O(n)$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search for the quantity $\mu(n)$ governing perturbation of multiply-covered convex plane curves into nondegenerate curves in $\mathbb{R}^n$, and the conjectured Frenet-frame length inequality involving $SO(2)\subset O(n)$, did not return any source resolving the question for general $n>3$. No paper announcing a determination of $\mu(n)$ or a proof/disproof of the length inequality was located, so the status remains unverified.

status_evidence.title: Frenet–Serret formulas - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Background on nondegenerate curves and Frenet frames in R^n; no information on μ(n).
status_evidence.claim: General references on Frenet frames do not address the specific quantity μ(n) or the proposed length inequality.
